subject: DPA: telemetry / KMS audit language for Micron Health
messages:
From: Sara Liang <sara.liang@micronhealth.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.com
Cc: legal@micronhealth.com
Date: Fri, 17 Apr 2027 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: DPA redline questions: telemetry, KV cache retention, and KMS audit

Hi Jonas,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Legal ran a quick pass on the DPA and sent a redline (attached). There are three items we need to close before we can proceed to procurement:

1) Telemetry / analytics: your team references "operational telemetry" in section 4. We need confirmation that telemetry will not contain customer PII or prompt content in plaintext, and we need the option to opt out of certain telemetry categories for our account.

2) KV cache / transient storage: the redline asks for clarity on how long cached prefixes (KV cache) are retained on SSD/NVMe and whether Micron Health can request immediate purge or a short retention window.

3) KMS / auditor access: our compliance team sometimes requires an external auditor to validate KMS key management and HSM attestations. The current language allows for "auditor access to production keys" which is a hard stop for us. We need either (A) an alternative where Redwood provides auditor reports and HSM attestation documents, or (B) a tightly-scoped, supervisor-reviewed process for in-place auditor verification without exposing plaintext.

I've attached the redline and a short spreadsheet with annotated asks. Can you route this to product + security and let me know what you can commit to? Procurement needs answers by end of next week to keep the timeline.

Attachments: Micron_DPA_Redline_v3.docx (docx), Redline_annotated_comments.xlsx (xlsx)

Thanks,
Sara Liang
Senior Counsel, Micron Health

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.com, dev.patel@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 17 Apr 2027 14:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: DPA redline questions: telemetry, KV cache retention, and KMS audit

Thanks for the ping. Quick security take and suggested compromise language below. High level: we cannot provide external auditors with access to plaintext customer keys or production HSM consoles. However, we can provide strong compensating artifacts and, in limited cases, supervised auditor sessions that preserve confidentiality.

Security answers / proposals:
- Telemetry: telemetry is operational (metrics, error traces, resource usage) and by default does NOT include full prompt or response payloads in plaintext. We do capture anonymized sampling for quality (configurable) and retain traces for 30 days by default. Proposed clause: "Operational telemetry excludes customer prompt/response content in plaintext. Customer may opt out of optional telemetry categories (sampling for model quality, anonymized traces) via account setting or written request."

- KV cache retention/purge: KV cache (in-memory + local NVMe spill) is transient and encrypted at rest. Typical retention window is up to 72 hours under normal load; we can support customer-specific TTLs down to 1 hour for dedicated or reserved instances. For hosted accounts, we can commit to a contractual purge-on-request SLA of 48 hours for cached prefixes. Proposed clause: "Redwood will purge customer-specific KV cache material within 48 hours of a written purge request for hosted accounts; dedicated deployments may elect shorter TTLs as configured in service settings."

- KMS / auditor: we will NOT grant direct access to live KMS keys or HSM consoles. Options we can offer: (1) provide current HSM attestation reports (e.g., CA/third-party certs) and our KMS key rotation & access logs for the relevant timeframe; (2) offer a supervised auditor session where Redwood staff execute agreed procedures in a controlled environment without exposing plaintext; (3) provide a SOC2+ supplement or AICPA report where applicable. Proposed contractual language: "Customer may request auditor verification of Redwood's KMS and HSM controls. Redwood will provide attestation reports, documented key management procedures, and, where necessary, a supervised auditor assessment under a mutually agreeable scope. Direct access to live key material or HSM consoles is not permitted."

I've attached a short text file with the proposed wording for security to hand to legal. Also flagged a requirement: if they insist on <vendor-level> third-party analytics access to raw payloads, that's a non-starter. We'll require those analytics providers to operate on anonymized or hashed derivatives only.

Next steps: Laura, if you can fold these suggestions into a DPA counter and propose a few toggles (48h purge vs 24h for dedicated), I can sign off and we can send back to Micron.

-Neha

[Attachment: security-response-proposal.txt (txt)]

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>

Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, neha.kapoor@redwood.com, dev.patel@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 14:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA redline questions: telemetry, KV cache retention, and KMS audit

Sara — thanks for the redline and the clear asks. Internal team reviewed and below is what we can offer as a starting point; Laura will follow with final counter language in the DPA tomorrow. If this looks acceptable, please let us know and we can circulate the redline + DocuSign path to procurement.

Summary of proposed commitments:
- Telemetry: Redwood confirms that operational telemetry excludes plaintext customer prompt/response content. We will add an opt-out for optional telemetry categories (sampling for model quality and anonymized traces) at account level.

- KV cache retention: For hosted accounts we can commit to purge-on-request with a 48-hour SLA. For dedicated deployments we can configure customer TTLs down to 1 hour.

- KMS / auditor: Redwood cannot grant external parties direct access to live KMS keys or HSM consoles. Instead we will provide attestation reports, documented key management procedures, and access logs for the relevant timeframe. If Micron requires further validation, Redwood will accommodate a supervised auditor assessment with an agreed scope that prevents exposure of plaintext or live keys.

If you confirm these three bullets are acceptable in principle, Laura will return a clean counter with specific clause text and we can get procurement/DocuSign moving. If Micron prefers the supervised assessment route for KMS as a mandatory condition, note that will require a brief operational runbook to schedule and scope the review.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call if helpful.

-Jonas Weber
